assignments.title: Contracts, incentives and organizations

canonical_specification.outcome: Solve simple principal-agent problems and evaluate incentive trade-offs.

owned_paths: content/projects/v05-c09-* (only if instruction needs an offline asset)
assignments.content: Teach principal/agent timing and hidden post-contract effort versus c08 hidden types; contractible outcome versus unverifiable action, utility/expected-profit objectives, reservation utility, IC and IR. Derive an original two-action/two-outcome optimal wage contract with full feasible/limited-liability/binding-constraint/global comparisons and observable-effort benchmark; distinguish risk-bearing from incentive rents, handle tie/implementation conditions and infeasible effort. Include monitoring with a solved informative signal or verifiable audit comparison and costs; explain why noisy performance and information about effort differ. Develop a solved multitask effort-allocation example showing that rewarding a measurable proxy can redirect effort from unmeasured value; avoid claiming all high incentives are bad. Explain firm boundaries using transaction costs, incomplete contracts, ownership/residual control and a concrete hold-up comparison, with model assumptions and no claim that integration removes every agency problem. At least three worked cases if needed for this scope, eight fully solved original exercises, teach-back and answered delayed check, inspected primary method records and an independent checker. Do not assume continuous-time contracting or general optimal-control tools. Graduate sufficient-statistic/general multitask/ownership theories are extension routes; current simple cases must be complete.

assignments.title: Externalities and public goods

canonical_specification.outcome: Compare corrective instruments under informational and institutional constraints.

owned_paths: content/projects/v05-c10-* (only if instruction needs an offline asset)
assignments.content: Teach external marginal versus private cost/benefit, social surplus/resource accounting and efficiency/distribution. Derive an original competitive external-cost quantity model and Pigouvian tax at the optimum, including revenue as transfer, incidence and damage/quantity uncertainty/measurement assumptions; compare a quantity instrument or standards using explicit cases, not a universal instrument ranking. Teach nonrivalry/nonexcludability, public-good vertical aggregation and Samuelson marginal-benefit sum with corner conditions; solve original voluntary-contribution Nash and efficient provision/financing, distinguishing public goods from common-pool congestion. Develop a solved congestion externality or toll example with own versus external cost and who pays/receives. Explain Coase bargaining conditional on clear/enforceable rights, feasible transfer/wealth, complete information, negligible transaction costs and bargaining implementation; solve an original transferable-surplus rights comparison and distinguish efficient allocation from distribution. At least three worked cases if needed, eight fully solved original exercises with transfer/proof/critique and delayed answer. No current legal/regulatory assertions. Primary methods inspected and exact independent checker; no general empirical causal/policy implementation inference from synthetic numbers.

assignments.title: Auctions, matching and market design

canonical_specification.outcome: Analyze allocation rules and incentive properties in designed markets.

owned_paths: content/projects/v05-c11-* (only if instruction needs an offline asset)
assignments.content: Define auction timing, private versus common values, risk neutrality, reserve/tie/payment rules and information; compare first-price, second-price, ascending and descending formats within scoped conditions. Fully prove second-price truthful weak dominance and original bid/payment examples; derive and globally verify an original symmetric iid-uniform first-price equilibrium, expected allocation/payments/revenue and revenue-equivalence conditions with envelope or explicitly scoped proof. Explain failures with risk aversion, asymmetric/correlated/common values, reserves and altered entry, without universal claims; distinguish bidder surplus and seller revenue. Define one-to-one matching/preferences, individual rationality, blocking pairs and stability; implement an original deferred-acceptance example both proposer directions with full termination/stability/proposer-optimal reasoning, honest strategy-proofness scope and distinction between stable and Pareto/total-surplus notions. Supply a fully proved strategy-proof serial-dictatorship or equivalent simple allocation mechanism; do not infer DA strategy-proofness merely from proposer optimality. Original eight solved exercises, at least three worked examples, answered delayed check, primary inspection and independent exact bid/deviation/matching enumeration checker. Graduate full general matching incentive proof can be an explicit recorded followup.

assignments.title: Behavioral economics and microeconomic evidence

canonical_specification.outcome: Evaluate departures from standard choice and the evidence needed to support interventions.

owned_paths: content/projects/v05-c12-* (only if instruction needs an offline asset)
assignments.content: Teach behavioral departures as precise hypotheses rather than a bias-name catalogue. Define reference-dependent value/loss aversion versus curvature/risk aversion, reference/endowment/choice-set assumptions and a solved original valuation/framing model with comparative predictions and identification limits. Define exponential versus quasi-hyperbolic discounting and solve an original finite-horizon present-bias/commitment example by actual date-specific choices, distinguishing naive and sophisticated beliefs and preference versus belief/constraint explanations. Treat selected cognitive biases (e.g. limited attention/default/status quo) with mechanisms and possible alternative rational explanations; no unsupported universal prevalence. Teach laboratory/field experiments, random assignment versus random sampling, attrition/noncompliance/demand effects/multiple testing, preregistration, measurement, uncertainty, external validity and replication versus reproducibility; build a small original randomized-example analysis with explicit assignment law, outcome calculations and complete inference warranted by design. Link prior Vol4 methods instead of re-teaching all regression. Explain why observed choices or welfare paternalism require a stated normative criterion (experienced/decision utility, long-run versus current self, informed stable choices); quantify a model intervention and identify distribution/information/implementation uncertainty. All empirical source claims must be primary, dated and precisely scoped; avoid contested findings as settled facts and no invented October2026 data. Eight fully solved original exercises and >=2 full worked cases (three appropriate for scope), source proposals and checker/author record; answered teach-back/retention. Root owns volume assessment and later synthesis, so do not label the whole volume accepted.
